name: Windows Pilot
description: Pilot a real Windows desktop from any agent in this workspace — list and focus windows, screenshot the screen, click, type and press keys — plus a Playwright that drives a persistent browser profile on that machine, so the agent works inside the user's own logged-in sessions. Reaches the machine through aw-remote-hosts; no fixed host, every setting is per-call overridable.

skills.description: Pilot a real Windows desktop reached through aw-remote-hosts — screenshot the screen, find and focus windows, click/type/press keys, and drive a persistent Playwright browser profile on that machine so the agent acts inside the user's own logged-in sessions. Use for anything about "my Windows machine", the Surface, piloting a Windows app, or automating a site in the user's own browser.

remote_backend_url.description: aw-backend base URL that fronts aw-remote-hosts, e.g. https://api.aw.tekflox.com. Every call goes through {url}/api/workspaces/{remote_workspace}/remote-hosts/{remote_host_id}/... . Set all three of remote_backend_url/remote_workspace/remote_token or none — with any one missing the tools fail naming exactly what is absent rather than guessing a host.

remote_workspace.description: The CALLING workspace's own slug (e.g. 'aw') — NOT the slug the target host happens to be registered under. aw-backend resolves host ownership server-side, so a host linked to a different workspace of yours is still reached via this workspace's own slug. Using the host's slug here returns 401.

remote_token.description: Bearer token for aw-backend — this workspace's AW_WORKSPACE_HOST_TOKEN (from the aw-remote-host /link handshake). Routed to the zero-knowledge secret store via POST /api/apps/windows-pilot/settings — never stored in plain config, because it can run arbitrary commands on a personal machine.

remote_host_id.description: Id of the linked WINDOWS host to pilot, from 'aw-workspace-cli remote-hosts hosts'. Its exec must run in the logged-in interactive session — win_pilot_status reports the session id so you can check. Defaults to Frederico's Surface (DESKTOP-DRMKFBT). Every tool accepts a per-call remote_host_id override.

python_exe.description: How to invoke Python on the Windows host. 'py -3' uses the Python launcher, which picks the newest install; use 'py -3.12' or a full path to pin one. The host agent needs 3.8+.

screenshot_dir.description: Directory on THIS workspace's filesystem where captured PNGs land, relative to the workspace root. Every capture accepts a local_path override.

browser.description: Which browser win_browser_launch starts on the host: 'edge' or 'chrome'. Falls back to whichever is actually installed.

browser_path.description: Optional full path to the browser executable, for a non-standard install.

browser_user_data_dir.description: Profile directory the piloted browser uses on the host. Defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA%\aw-windows-pilot\browser-profile — a persistent profile, so sites the user signs into once in that window stay signed in for the agent. Chrome 136+ and current Edge refuse remote debugging on the browser's DEFAULT profile, so pointing this at the user's everyday profile does not work.

cdp_port.description: Localhost port the piloted browser exposes CDP on. Only ever bound on the host's own loopback interface.

apps.reason: This app contributes an mcp.json entry (the 'aw-windows-pilot' server) that MCP Gateway discovers and merges; without the gateway no agent can reach its tools.

dependencies.note: Runtime-enforced app dependency: aw-workspace loads mcp-gateway before this app so the gateway can scan windows-pilot/mcp.json.
